target_zone_range.note: BONAP was used as the primary county-level authority. For the project threshold, Hays County is supported by the Purola Preserve flora and recent Hays County field documentation; Travis County is supported by the UT Plant Resources Center herbarium index; Bandera County is independently supported by a documented Lost Maples photograph. Additional prior working counties are retained separately until individually rechecked.

morphology_keys.habit: Herbaceous perennial from stout rootstocks; stems usually clustered, ascending to somewhat decumbent, about 20–60 cm tall.
morphology_keys.leaf_arrangement: Leaves crowded along the stems; generally alternate/irregularly spaced.
morphology_keys.leaf_morphology: Lanceolate to linear-lanceolate, about 1–3 cm wide, usually narrowly acuminate; often visibly narrower than A. viridis.
morphology_keys.inflorescence: Terminal, usually solitary, many-flowered and very crowded; peduncle length varies.
morphology_keys.flower_color: Pale yellowish-green, sometimes purple-flushed; corona may show darker purple hoods.
morphology_keys.gynostegium_detail: Corona hoods contain horns; hood color and peduncle length vary among forms/subspecies.
morphology_keys.fruit: Paired or solitary follicles; mature pods split to release comose seeds.
morphology_keys.joey_field_note: In Edwards Plateau Botany Part II, Joey shows a clear flowering umbel and uses the flower cluster to reinforce milkweed corona/hood structure.

field_diagnostics.separation_from_viridis: TPWD emphasizes leaf shape: A. asperula usually has lanceolate to linear-lanceolate leaves with narrowly acuminate tips, while A. viridis has broader oblong to ovate leaves with obtuse to shortly acute tips. A. asperula also extends farther west in Texas.

ecological_notes.habitat: Rocky and sandy prairies of the Blackland Prairie, Edwards Plateau, Grand Prairie, Rolling Plains, High Plains and Trans-Pecos.
ecological_notes.central_texas_note: Well documented in Hays County and elsewhere across the Edwards Plateau / Central Texas.
ecological_notes.host_status: An important native monarch larval host in Texas; also supports other milkweed-associated insects and pollinators.
